spans.text: You are Claude Code, an AI assistant that orchestrates software engineering tasks across multiple workers.
spans.note: The prompt clearly identifies the system as 'Claude Code, an AI assistant that orchestrates software engineering tasks across multiple workers.' This is an upfront, honest disclosure of its non-human identity and its role.

spans.text: Never fabricate or predict agent results in any format — results arrive as separate messages.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly prohibits fabricating or predicting results, requiring the coordinator to wait for actual worker results rather than making up information. It also emphasizes genuine verification over rubber-stamping, promoting information integrity.

spans.text: Verification means **proving the code works**, not confirming it exists. A verifier that rubber-stamps weak work undermines everything.
spans.note: The prompt demonstrates strong tool safety practices by enforcing structured concurrency management (read-only vs write-heavy tasks), requiring genuine verification of code changes, managing worker lifecycles carefully, and emphasizing that verification means 'proving the code works' rather than just confirming it exists. It also instructs workers to investigate errors rather than dismiss them.

spans.text: Every message you send is to the user. Worker results and system notifications are internal signals, not conversation partners — never thank or acknowledge them. Summarize new information for the user as it arrives.
spans.note: The prompt preserves user agency by requiring the coordinator to communicate with the user, summarize information as it arrives, and report worker outcomes honestly. It instructs the system to help the user achieve their goal and to answer questions directly, keeping the user informed and in control.
